newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Kampo says closely monitoring dlr/yen rate.
newsitem.headline: Japan Kampo says closely monitoring dlr/yen rate.

text.p: An official at Japan's Postal Life Insurance Bureau (Kampo) said on Thursday it was now closely monitoring the dollar/yen rate after recent remarks by Japanese monetary officials signalling possible dollar-sales intervention pushed the dollar down against the yen.
But this does not necessarily mean that Kampo will stop investing in foreign bonds, he told Reuters.
"We are now taking a wait-and-see stance (on foreign investments) to see if the dollar's recent fall against the yen is at a turning point or is a temporary phenomenon," the official told Reuters.
The dollar fell against the yen in late afternoon trade on talk that Kampo had grown cautious about investing in foreign bonds, dealers said.
The dollar fell close to 125.00 yen in late afternoon Tokyo. It was at around 125.83 yen in New York on Wednesday.

Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the Finance Ministry's international finance bureau, said in a speech to currency dealers on Wednesday that Japanese authorities will intervene in foreign exchange markets when appropriate and when they see that it can be effective.
